newsitem.title: JAPAN: US powdered metallurgy car part makers lobby Japan.
newsitem.headline: US powdered metallurgy car part makers lobby Japan.

text.p: A trade mission of American powdered metallurgy (P/M) autoparts makers is visiting Japan from Monday until Friday to seek to increase the use of powdered metallurgy parts in Japanese cars exported to or made in North America, the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo said on Monday.

The mission, supported by the U.S. Department of Commerce and the Japan External Trade Organisation (JETRO), will hold individual meetings this week with representatives of member companies of the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association and the Japan Auto Parts Industries Association in Tokyo, Nagoya and Osaka.
Powdered Metallurgy offers improved efficiency in the production of precision metal parts such as engine parts, transmission, brakes, steering and suspension systems.
P/M parts help carmakers reduce weight and increase fuel efficiency, and they are recyclable, the embassy said.
The average Japanese car contains 6.64 kg of P/M parts, while North American cars contain up to 18.1 kg, which is expected to rise to 22.7 kg by the year 2000.
